items.original: HYROX is built to be accessible. If you can walk, lunge, carry and push, you already have the foundation. The difference between a beginner and an elite athlete isn't the movements — it's pacing, consistency and reps.

items.original: For more than 25 years AJ has dedicated his career to understanding the human body and unlocking its potential through science-based training, nutrition and performance coaching.

items.original: A current HYROX Pro Athlete and former elite cyclist with Team AEG Toshiba, AJ founded a Human Performance Studio in 2010 specialising in VO2 analysis, metabolic testing and body composition. He has coached with Gainesville Health & Fitness, Life Time Fitness, Go Primal, Primal Health and Performance, and OneLife Fitness.

items.where: div · Is HYROX good for beginners?
items.original: Yes. The movements in HYROX are deliberately basic — there are no barbell lifts, no gymnastics, and nothing that requires months of technique work. If you can walk, lunge, carry and push, you already have the foundation. What separates a beginner from an elite athlete is pacing, consistency and reps, not skill.

items.original: How is HYROX different from CrossFit?
items.text: How is HYROX different from CrossFit?

items.where: div · How is HYROX different from CrossFit?
items.original: CrossFit varies every day and includes technical Olympic lifts. HYROX is the same every single time, with simple movements — and roughly half of a HYROX race is running. That repeatability is exactly what makes it useful as a training method: you always know what is coming, so you can measure whether you are getting faster.
